messages:
Alex: Heads-up — noticed a spike in late ingest for EU shards (tenant 8421). Stale agg-hours for a few cohorts. Can we discuss a targeted reprocess path that won't blow our quota pool? :eyes:
Maria: Which cohorts/shards specifically? I saw anomalies in /dash/telemetry->agg-hours yesterday but didn't dig in.
Alex: 8421:{shard-3,shard-7}, 9102:shard-1. Late window ~3h behind. We should avoid full rehydrate. Thinking: small targeted rerun + kv-prefix caching to avoid full model misses.
Sam: Agree with targeted. Two questions: 1) can console trigger per-tenant small-window reprocess (UI flag)? 2) how many tokens will that burn against replay quota?
Irene: On (1) we have a dry-run toggle in the console but it only supports full-tenant runs. We could add a "windowed" mode but that's UX+api work. On (2) estimate ~2.5k ops for shard-3 window if we keep batch_size=256.
Jordan: If we add a windowed mode, we need routing rules so small runs go to the low-latency reserved pool, not the spot backlog. Otherwise they'll get queued for days.
Maria: Routing policy change seems heavy. Could we instead tag the job with priority=interactive and have the scheduler honor priority weights? Minimal infra changes.
Sam: Priority weights help, but quota accounting still matters. If multiple small runs happen concurrently we'll eat the tenant's replay quota and risk crossing global quota. We should add a per-run ephemeral token consumption estimate in the UI before triggering.
Alex: Good call. UX asks: show estimated cost + estimated time, then a confirm button. Also add an "auto-cancel" if system rejects due to quota.
Irene: From infra side: we can implement a conservative estimator (max_records * per-record-cost) and a preflight check API: POST /reprocess/preflight -> {accepted: bool, estimate: n}. Minimal change.
Sam: API debate: should preflight live in the public console API or be an internal-only endpoint? If public, customers could script it; if internal, it keeps us flexible. Leaning internal-first, then expose.
Jordan: Internal-first makes sense. Also suggest a routing fallback: if reserved pool is saturated, fall back to a lower-cost compute variant that runs slower but bounded. We already have those variants for hosted models.
Maria: Can we add a dashboard signal so SRE/ops get notified when targeted reprocesses spike? Right now dash only shows total reprocesses per day. We need per-tenant spikes + queue depth.
Alex: +1 for per-tenant spikes. If replay-bot can emit an alert when preflight reject rate > 5% in 10m window, that would be actionable.
replay-bot: PRECHECK for tenant 8421: preflight estimate 2.6k ops, accepted=true, routed=reserved-pool-5, eta=6m. (build 2026-03-21/rv.31) :white_check_mark:
Irene: Nice — routing header now returned by preflight. We should persist that in the job metadata so the console shows where it landed.
Sam: Edge case: what if preflight accepted but during run quota is consumed by something else and it fails mid-run? We should implement a lease/token that reserves estimated quota for 60s and then renews periodically. If renew fails, job cancels gracefully.
Jordan: Lease approach aligns with queue-runbook flow. Add a handshake: POST /reprocess/start returns lease_id; POST /reprocess/keepalive renews. Keepalive cadence = 45s.
Maria: UX: show lease status live in the job detail panel (green/renewing / yellow/renew-wait / red/expired). Also show the original estimate and actual consumption post-run.
Alex: Ops question: do we want an automatic canary for aggregates? i.e., reprocess a 1% sample of affected tenant first and run the aggregate diff check against canonical metrics before continuing.
Irene: Yes. I can add a canary flag to preflight: canary_pct=1. Preflight will return canary_job_id and a comparator path. We'll produce a small metrics diff.
Sam: Comparator should be deterministic: delta % on agg-hours, plus sample-level hashes so we guard against nondeterministic ops. If drift > threshold, auto-stop.
Maria: Sounds good. Who wants to own the console work? I can take the preflight UI and job detail additions. Will sync with Irene for API contract.
Alex: I'll draft the preflight API spec and canary schema. Sam and Jordan can review routing/fallback sections. Let's aim for a small rollout: internal-only for two weeks, monitor via the new dashboard signal, then expose interactive reprocess to SREs.
Jordan: Timeline OK. Quick follow-up: Sam, can you mock the quota estimator numbers by EOD? Maria, I'll make a small wireframe for the job detail.
Sam: Yep — will post numbers and a tiny script to simulate concurrent runs by 6pm PST.
Maria: Wireframe incoming. :thumbsup:
Alex: Thanks everyone. We'll reconvene after the preflight draft. /cc @replay-bot for alerts subscription setup.
